title: Regional & Tiered Fallback Activation Decider for Overload Signals
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We need a deterministic, observable component that decides when to activate fallback model variants or route traffic across regions/tiers in response to overload indicators (HTTP 429 surge, sustained timeouts, elevated error rate). Current heuristics are decentralized and produce flapping and unexpected customer-visible throttles during regional capacity spikes.

Goal: Ship an "activation decider" service that consumes multi-signal overload telemetry, applies smoothing/hysteresis, and emits a single activation decision per route+customer+region. The decider should support: (1) configurable signal weighting (429 rate, p95 latency, timeout count, error-rate), (2) per-tier and per-region thresholds with decay windows, (3) minimum stable hold periods and cooldown/backoff before re-enabling, and (4) a clear audit trail for each activation decision to be surfaced in Console and incident debug flows.
acceptance_criteria: Activation decisions produced for all routes in staging based on combined signal score (429s, timeouts, error-rate, p95) with configurable weights
No more than 1% additional false-positive activations (simulated by historical replay) compared to manual baseline
Console shows activation events with causal signals and re-enable timestamps for 30 days
Rollback and manual-override path in routing policy that can disable automatic activations per-customer or per-region
tech_notes:
Design summary: compute a rolling "overload score" S = sum(w_i * normalized(signal_i)) over 1s granularity, then apply exponential smoothing with decay factor alpha. Trigger = S > T_activate for window W_activate and hold for H_min before re-evaluating. Re-enable only after S < T_release for W_release and exponential backoff on repeated activations.

Signals: normalized 429-rate (reqs with 429 / total reqs), p95 latency normalized to target latency, connection/response timeouts (absolute counts per 10s), and downstream model error-rate (invalid responses, OOMs).

Variant mapping: routing table contains ordered fallback variants: primary -> fast-quantized -> regional-fallback -> remote-fallback. Activation decision should attach chosen variant and rationalization code to route request header for tracing.

Observability: emit activation_event with {route, customer, region, tier, S, signals, threshold, reason_code, decision_ts} to metrics pipeline and audit log. Add a synthetic replay tool to validate decisions against historical traces.
implementation_plan: 1) Add overloaded-signal ingestion in routing-proxy (instrument 429, timeout counts, p95 windows) - ENG infra
2) Implement activation-decider microservice with config API and rule store
3) Integrate decider with routing-control-plane (policy evaluation hook) to apply variant mapping
4) Add activation events to telemetry (metrics + audit log) and wire Console UI panel
5) Create canary: enable automatic activations for non-critical routes in eu-west-1 with manual overrides
6) Run 48h historical replay against past incidents and adjust weights/thresholds
testing_plan: Unit tests for scoring and smoothing logic (edge cases: sparse traffic, sudden spikes)
Integration tests: end-to-end with routing-proxy to ensure headers and policy changes flow correctly
Chaos test: simulated regional capacity drop (20% replicas offline) in staging to validate fallbacks
Load test: synthetic 429 flood to verify no flapping and correct hold/re-enable behavior
Customer safety: dry-run mode to log decisions without routing changes for 72h before gradual enable
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): deploy decider+proxy instrumentation to staging clusters; run replay and tune thresholds (1 week)
Phase 2 (canary): enable for a subset of low-impact routes in eu-west-1 for 48h (manual ops guard)
Phase 3 (regional gradual): enable automatic activations in a single region for P1/P2 customers with telemetry monitoring (7 days)
Phase 4 (global): full enable with per-customer opt-out and SLO alerts if activation rate > expected baseline
risks: Overly aggressive thresholds could degrade customer quality by selecting lower-quality model variants
Insufficient signal smoothing may cause repeated oscillation (flapping) across enable/disable
Audit/log volume increase could affect metrics storage costs
Cross-region signal correlation: local transient spikes may be misinterpreted if global signals are not considered
